implementation_notes: TypeScript's god object is a mega-interface (`IApplicationService` with sixty members) implemented by one class and injected by token through a DI container — and `any` inside the implementation erases the very type information that would have made the fan-out visible. The structural counters are the type system itself: `unknown` instead of `any` forces narrowing, and declaring the narrow interface at the point of consumption (`interface UserReader { find(id: string): Promise<User> }`) means the god class can be deleted once nothing depends on its wide shape. `noUnusedLocals` plus an import graph view (`madge --image`) surfaces which modules route through the god service.
idiom_name: IApplicationService mega-interface plus DI container provider
pitfalls: `any` on one field of the god service removes the compiler's ability to complain about the fan-out it was meant to reveal.
Declaration merging across files can grow a module's exported surface invisibly — the same failure mode as C++ `partial` classes.
`as` casts between the wide and narrow shapes reintroduce the coupling that the narrow interface was meant to remove.
